title: EU Foreign Ministers Formally Reject Schröder as Ukraine Security Mediator
detail: EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels unanimously rejected Putin's proposal to use former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder as a mediator in future Ukraine security talks. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas was blunt: Schröder 'worked as a high-level lobbyist for Russian state-owned companies' and would effectively be 'sitting on both sides of the table.' Ukraine also rejected the idea. The episode highlighted the EU's hardened stance against Russian diplomatic maneuvers that exploit personal ties to former European leaders.

media.caption: EU's Kallas rules out Schröder as Ukraine mediator, saying he is effectively a Russian lobbyist

title: Germany and Ukraine Launch 'Brave Germany' €4B Defense Package with Deep-Strike Drones
detail: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius traveled to Kyiv and signed a landmark joint defense agreement branded the 'Brave Germany' arms program. The centerpiece is joint production of long-range 'Deep Strike' drones with a range of up to 1,500 km, along with 5,000 AI-enabled medium-range strike drones for Ukrainian forces. The broader package totals €4 billion and includes Patriot missile systems, 36 IRIS-T launchers, and €300 million specifically for Ukrainian deep-strike capabilities. The deal came days after Trump cancelled a planned US Tomahawk missile deployment to Germany, accelerating Berlin's drive for European autonomous strike capacity.

media.caption: Defense Minister Pistorius in Kyiv unveils 'Brave Germany' joint drone production and €4B arms package

title: Rheinmetall Announces Domestic Cruise Missile Production to Fill US Tomahawk Gap
detail: Germany's largest arms manufacturer Rheinmetall announced plans to begin producing cruise missiles domestically at its main facility in Unterlüß, Lower Saxony. The announcement followed the US cancellation of a planned Tomahawk cruise missile deployment to Germany. Berlin is simultaneously evaluating European alternatives including a land-based derivative of the French MdCN (Naval Cruise Missile) and a Taurus NEO extended-range concept. The move represents a significant step in Germany's strategic shift toward European autonomous strike capability, accelerated by the breakdown in transatlantic defense cooperation under Trump.

media.caption: Rheinmetall plans domestic cruise missile production at Unterlüß to compensate for cancelled US Tomahawk deployment

title: Forsa Poll: AfD Leads CDU/CSU by 5 Points — Would Win 196 Bundestag Seats
detail: The May 11 Forsa poll showed the AfD at 27%, CDU/CSU at 22%, Greens at 15%, SPD at 12%, Die Linke at 11%, and FDP at 4% — below the 5% Bundestag threshold. In projected seat distribution, AfD would hold 196 seats versus CDU/CSU's 159, making the far-right party the largest force in parliament. The poll confirmed the trend from earlier May INSA polls and came as the constitutional court proceedings over the AfD's 'confirmed extremist' designation by the domestic intelligence agency (BfV) remained unresolved. All mainstream parties maintain their 'Brandmauer' (firewall) against coalition with the AfD.

media.caption: Forsa May 11, 2026 poll: AfD 27% leads CDU/CSU 22% — AfD projected largest party in Bundestag
